executiveSummary: Severe, prolonged flooding in Thailand has killed at least 31 people and affected more than 3.5 million, with authorities warning of continued heavy rain and flash-flood risk. View Article IFRC reporting confirms widespread, ongoing flooding across 30 provinces in Thailand, with over 3.3 million people affected and about 8,000 displaced as relief operations continue. Supporting Report A lethal earthquake on Indonesia's Flores Island caused at least 68 deaths, over 200 injuries, roughly 19,000 people displaced, and extensive damage to homes, health facilities, schools, and roads. View Article Nepal's flood emergencies remain active, including a flash-flood response targeting 28,000 people in Rasuwa under an ongoing emergency appeal. Supporting Report An ongoing IFRC earthquake operation in Colombia continues to target affected communities, with a defined appeal framework still in place. Supporting Report A high-fatality avalanche at Mount Himlung, Nepal, killed 15 Nepali workers, left one missing, and forced a pause of recovery operations due to continued mountain hazards. View Article In the U.S. state of New Mexico, flooding prompted evacuations and emergency assistance amid concerns about a minor dam and additional rainfall. View Article Assessment: Flooding remains the dominant global hazard this week, with the most acute humanitarian footprint in Thailand and sustained response requirements in Nepal and Ecuador. Earthquake impacts remain significant in Indonesia and operationally relevant in Colombia.

outlook72h: Thailand: Continued heavy rain in some regions could trigger additional flash flooding and exacerbate ongoing inundation. View Article Mexico Pacific Coast (Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Jalisco): Very heavy rain, flooding, dangerous surf, and landslide risk remain possible as a Pacific system influences the region. View Article Central U.S. (incl. Texas/Oklahoma): Additional storms may bring urban flooding and isolated severe weather including tornado potential in affected corridors. View Article U.S. West Coast: Elevated sea levels sustain a background risk of coastal flooding and erosion during high tides and storm events. View Article
regionalTrends: Americas: Earthquake operations persist in Colombia, while the U.S. Southwest/central regions continue to face episodic flood risks following tropical moisture intrusions.
Pacific hurricane season: Elevated rainfall and coastal hazards threaten parts of Mexico's Pacific coast; authorities highlight flood and landslide risks.
Mountain and alpine environments: Nepal's avalanche event underscores seasonal instability that can abruptly disrupt operations and access.
